chunks: Although, by Allah, doubt has certainly overtook and certainty entered,
so it seems as if what was guaranteed to you has become obligatory upon you, and as if what was obligatory upon you has been lifted from you.
So hasten to action, and fear the suddenness of death,
for the return of age is not hoped for as the return of livelihood is hoped for,
whatever is missed from livelihood today, its increase is hoped for tomorrow, but whatever is lost from age yesterday, its return is not hoped for today.
"Fear Allah as He ought to be feared and do not die except while you are Muslims."
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of hastening to good deeds in light of the uncertainty of death?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) illustrates the psychological tension between doubt and certainty to urge immediate action, highlighting that while material sustenance can be replenished, time is an irreversible asset. This reflection on the urgency of *amal* (deeds) before the suddenness of death (*baghata al-ajal*) is grounded in the Quranic command to maintain true piety until the final breath.
